assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins established, by quantitative kinetics on ruthenium-modified proteins, that electron tunneling through the polypeptide is governed by distance and driving force in a Marcus-type picture. It explains in physical terms how respiratory and photosynthetic enzymes move electrons, and it underlies my own field of biological energy conversion. The mechanism is stated cleanly, the originality is high, and the influence on bioenergetics and bioinorganic chemistry is lasting.
assessment.attribution: The credited pair is compact and fits two laureates. Gray and Winkler led the photo-triggered protein electron-transfer experiments. Credit for the underlying theory (Marcus, already recognised in 1992) and for related work by others, such as Dutton's empirical tunneling rules, would have to be handled carefully in the motivation.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation across many proteins and enzymes, with stable interpretation. Recognition is, if anything, long overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as Marcus-theory application rather than a new discovery; Dutton's parallel work is not in the credited names and is a priority question I cannot settle from the supplied text; my recall of details is from memory, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a central chemical mechanism in respiration, photosynthesis and water oxidation, and the work gives it a physical framework (concerted versus stepwise pathways, proton tunneling, vibronic theory) plus molecular electrocatalysis. This is exactly the kind of fundamental mechanism that connects biological energy conversion with synthetic catalysis, and I consider it important and original.
assessment.attribution: Four people are credited and only three can be named. Meyer is the early conceptual pioneer, Mayer developed the concerted hydrogen-atom and PCET thermochemistry, and Hammes-Schiffer supplied the theory. Nocera's contributions, especially on artificial photosynthesis and PCET in proteins, are left out of this proposal, so the allocation is open to dispute.
assessment.maturity: Well established and supported by independent experiment and theory over three decades. The field is mature, although the 'discovery' is a body of work rather than one event.
uncertainties: The candidacy rests on a line of work rather than one clearly attributable discovery; the choice of three among four strong contributors is genuinely ambiguous.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase catalyses biological nitrogen fixation at the FeMo-cofactor, one of the most remarkable metalloenzyme active sites. Structures revealing the cofactor, its interstitial carbide and the electron-delivery protein complex, together with the mechanistic enzymology, make it a deep problem in bioinorganic and structural chemistry with obvious planetary significance.
assessment.attribution: Rees solved the first structures, Einsle established the central carbide atom and later structures, and Seefeldt represents the mechanistic and kinetic enzymology. Dean, Ribbe and others made important contributions that cannot fit within three; Hoffman, Burgess and Howard are not on the supplied list, so the set is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: The structural picture is well established, but the catalytic mechanism, notably how N2 binds and how the E4 state turns over, is still being worked out. Recognition of the structure is mature; recognition of the mechanism may be premature.
uncertainties: Allocation across Rees, Einsle, Dean, Ribbe and Seefeldt is unresolved; the committee would need expert reports to weigh priority between structural and mechanistic work; mechanism details remain debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The idea that cells organise biochemistry through liquid-liquid phase separation into condensates has changed how cellular chemistry is thought about, and it has a clear physical-chemical basis in polymer demixing. The conceptual influence is very large and the originality is real.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman reported the liquid-like P granules, and Rosen demonstrated multivalent-interaction phase separation in reconstituted systems. Pappu and Mittag contributed essential physical and sequence-grammar understanding, so the choice of three leaves out important people.
assessment.maturity: The concept is widely adopted but still debated on mechanism, on what counts as true phase separation in vivo, and on how condensates function. The field may be somewhat early for a prize.
uncertainties: Controversy over in vivo relevance and the functional roles of condensates; whether the work is chemistry rather than cell biology; the three-laureate limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs lets proteins carry designed unnatural amino acids in living cells. It is a general chemical-biology tool with clear originality and major lasting influence on protein mechanism studies, imaging and engineering.
assessment.attribution: Schultz developed the first orthogonal systems and the evolution of synthetases in vivo. Chin extended this to eukaryotes, to quadruplet codons and to orthogonal ribosomes, and Wang was an early co-developer in Schultz's group. Yokoyama and Mehl also contributed, so the allocation is not completely clear.
assessment.maturity: The method is widely used, independently reproduced and mature, and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority questions among Schultz's former students and independent groups; as a method, the Nobel motivation could be judged narrower than a fundamental discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers makes it possible to record diffraction before radiation damage and to follow time-resolved structural changes. It makes dynamic processes in enzymes visible, a method I value, and it opened structures of small and difficult crystals.
assessment.attribution: Hajdu proposed and framed the diffraction-before-destruction concept, Chapman led the first demonstrations, and Schlichting contributed time-resolved and enzyme applications. Fromme and Spence and others played large roles in the first experiments and are omitted here, so allocation is very uncertain.
assessment.maturity: The technique is proven but still developing, and its impact on chemistry is so far limited to a modest set of systems. Possibly somewhat early.
uncertainties: The dependence on large facilities and a small number of high-impact results so far; unclear who is decisive among a big group of pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass-spectrometry proteomics methods, from shotgun and quantitative approaches to targeted and large-scale analysis, made systematic identification and quantification of proteins possible. The methodological impact on biochemistry and biology is very large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Six names are supplied. Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the plausible central figures for large-scale, quantitative and shotgun strategies. Hunt, Gygi and Heck also made decisive contributions, and the ionization methods themselves were recognised in 2002, so the configuration is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely adopted and independently confirmed. The question is mainly attribution within a crowded field.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be seen as a methods recognition overlapping with 2002 ionization work; the three-laureate limit against several equally strong contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional solution NMR methods and relaxation approaches extended structure and, importantly, dynamics determination to large biomolecules and complexes. They give a physical view of motion and conformational exchange that complements cryo-EM and crystallography.
assessment.attribution: Kay, Bax and Clore are the principal developers of heteronuclear multidimensional and TROSY-based approaches and dynamics methods. Wagner and Palmer are also credited, and the 2002 Wüthrich prize already recognised NMR structure determination, so the new element must be defined carefully.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed. Timeliness is acceptable, although the prize could be viewed as an incremental extension of earlier recognised work.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize; whether the contribution is a single clearly attributable discovery or a line of methodological development.
